findings.title: Narrowing the exported cache-key helper breaks existing callers
findings.explanation: The base API accepted any string member ID, while the current head requires the newly branded MemberId. A previously valid TypeScript call such as memberCacheKey(tenantId, "MEM-123456") now fails type checking even though the value satisfies the documented format. Because branding is compile-time-only and cache-key construction itself has unchanged runtime semantics, this change creates a source-incompatible public contract without a compatibility path or coordinated caller migration. Preserve compatibility by accepting and parsing a string internally, or migrate every consumer in the same change.
findings.failurePath: An existing caller passes a validated plain string to memberCacheKey; TypeScript checks it against MemberId, rejects the missing nominal brand, and prevents that caller or package from compiling.
